points.description: States that the problem is divided (split/broken down) into smaller subproblems (smaller instances of the same problem), using the term 'subproblems' or an exact equivalent such as 'smaller instances of the same problem'.
points.partial_credit: Half marks if only 'divide/break into smaller parts' is said without saying they are subproblems of the same problem.

points.description: States that the subproblems are solved recursively (the same method is applied to each subproblem, until a base case is reached or the subproblems are small enough to solve directly).
points.partial_credit: Half marks if 'solve the subproblems' is stated but recursion is not mentioned.

points.description: States that the solutions to the subproblems are combined (merged) into a solution for the original problem.
points.partial_credit: Half marks if 'combine the results' is stated without saying it produces the solution to the original problem.

rubric.notes: Full marks need all three steps (divide into subproblems, solve recursively, combine into the original solution) stated precisely with the correct terms. Vague wording such as 'split it up and do each part' earns nothing for that step; only clearly more than half of a step earns half marks. Any wrong statement about a step (for example, saying the parts are solved independently of recursion, or that they are not combined) loses that point. Examples such as merge sort do not replace the description.
